extracted.intended_audience: educated lay readers and seekers of natural theology; skeptics/atheists being addressed by a natural-philosophy/theological apologist
extracted.subtask_description: A series of arguments (natural theology) that infer a wise, directing God from observations about the smallness, number, behaviour and laws governing particles and natural phenomena (water, air, fire, cohesion, gravity, etc.). The text marshals experimental examples, biblical citations, and philosophical reasoning to show these regularities imply design and providence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument from order and regularity versus chance
rubrics_metrics.description: If all is deduced from mere chance, how can so steady an Order and Regularity, prevailing for many ages among so many millions, be derived from Chance whose very essence operates without Order?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This dimension challenges purely chance-based accounts by contrasting observed global order with the supposed disorder of chance; the text invites readers to consider that uncaused chance cannot account for long-enduring regularities and thus points to a directing Cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument from rains and watery particles (watry atoms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate a God from the Rains and Floods of Waters; the true God is distinguished from idols because idols cannot cause rain or give showers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses biblical references (e.g., Psalm and Jeremiah citations) and the observation that clouds and rain consist of innumerable small particles/drops. The text notes that the Scriptures praise God for covering the heavens with clouds and preparing rain, and argues that the origin and orderly distribution of rain require divine causation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument from the smallness and number of water particles
rubrics_metrics.description: The smallness and consequently the number of watry particles (drops) are such that clouds drop and distil abundantly upon man; the immense multiplicity of these minute particles points to design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text cites scriptural passages and observational claims about the vast number of droplets making up rain/clouds and argues that quantity and fineness themselves are evidence of divine greatness and ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument from the smallness and multiplicity of particles of air
rubrics_metrics.description: Air is a collection of innumerable diversities of small parts whose interactions produce enormous effects (storms, tempests, thunder, lightning); such forces arising from minute floating particles suggest a directing Wisdom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invites the skeptic to consider the power produced when innumerable aerial particles act together (e.g., storms) and to conclude that it is implausible these 'aerial armies' are moved by chance without destroying the world; appeals to historical accounts of storm effects to reinforce the point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument from the smallness and power of particles of fire/light
rubrics_metrics.description: Fire and light consist of inconceivably small and numerous particles whose collective powers are terrible (lightning causing earthquakes, burning mountains, cities destroyed); these powers imply restraint and direction by a superior power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives empirical magnification (e.g., from candle flame particle counts) and comparisons with lightning, the sun and stars; argues that since these numerous particles do not set the world on fire, they must be restrained by a superior power. References optical experiments (Newton's optics) to show particles' strict obedience to laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument from microscopic composition of living and inert bodies (all visible things composed of innumerable particles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plants, animals and minerals are composed of very small vessels, tubes, fat/oleaginous parts, and innumerable particles (as seen under microscopes and in chemical analysis); this invisible multiplicity and complexity shows the necessity of an intelligent cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draws on micrography (Leuwenhoeck), chemistry (extraction into air, fire, salt, spirit, earth), and the analogy of a painter: a complex landscape made of mixed colours requires a skilful artist, so too the world requires a wise artificer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of great bodies into small particles before usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Great bodies are generally first broken/divided into small particles before being fit for their uses (e.g., water must be fluid and divided rather than ice; fire must be liberated from combustible matter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses examples: ice vs. water, fire locked in wood/coal, gunpowder only effective when particles are freed. The point supports the providential ordering in which the Creator arranges matter by subdividing it to render it useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law/power of cohesion as evidence of design
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohesion: certain determinate kinds of atoms adhere to one another to produce particular effects; the variety and appropriateness of cohesion (e.g., tongue vs. teeth) manifest infinite wisdom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that cohesion is not merely rest; experimental references (Marriotte, Huygens) show bodies resist disturbance and that cohesion has great force. The variety of cohesion suited to function (soft blankets vs. hard wood analogy) is presented as evidence against chance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law/power of separation (putrefaction/fermentation) as evidence of design
rubrics_metrics.description: Separation: parts that cohere in one context obey other laws to separate (fermentation/putrefaction), enabling recycling of matter into fruitful earth and new forms; this cyclical separation shows wise governance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that without separation the world would be clogged with corpses and decay; the lawful alternation of cohesion and separation is cited as part of a wise system producing beneficial results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law/power of unattrition (persistence of fine particles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fine and tender particles have continued for many ages without attrition despite innumerable frictions, percussions and motions; their persistence (and/or balanced reproduction) implies providential regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenges the skeptic to explain how particles of fire, air and water preserve necessary forms despite violent motions and contacts; proposes either an unattrition law or regulated replenishment as evidence of divine providence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental powers: percussion, attraction and repulsion as laws of nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Percussion (collisions) and Attraction (with Repulsion consequentially) are principal powers by which bodies move and interact; the innumerable percussions and strict obedience to mathematical rules require explanation beyond chance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References experimental/mathematical work by Wallis, Wren, Huygens, Mariotte and Newton. Gives examples of paradoxical augmentations of motion (Huygens' chain example) and argues that the precise, law-like behaviour of countless collisions suggests a directing intelligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument from gravity and its beneficial effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Gravity (tendency to the center) is a ubiquitous law producing countless beneficial phenomena (sea pressure, rivers, rainfall, navigation, pumps, circulation of water, etc.) and thereby evidences a wise, gracious God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists many practical effects of gravity on earthly life (sea remaining on its bottom, rivers flowing, rain descending, fire and smoke rising, pumps, fountains). Argues that such a simple universal law yielding manifold goods is strong evidence of providential design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of gravitation to heavenly bodies as evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Observations suggest the law of gravity extends throughout the visible universe: heavenly bodies gravitate toward one another (planets about the sun, satellites about primaries), as in Newtonian astronomy; this universal regularity supports the argument for orderly design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes that planetary motion follows elliptical paths and that many astronomers accept such regularities; the text is cautious about relying solely on philosophers' opinions but points to observable regular motion as further evidence of design.
